newsitem.title: INDIA: India sees future needs met by new fuel reserves.
newsitem.headline: India sees future needs met by new fuel reserves.

text.p: India hopes to meet all its future energy needs by the exploitation of recently-discovered reserves of new hydrocarbon fuels, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

Vijay Kelkar, the top civil servant in the Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry, said the country has huge reserves of gas hydrates and coal-bed methane, which could reasonably be expected to meet all the nation's energy needs in the future.

"India has large, mind-boggling reserves of gas hydrates," Kelkar told delegates to a two-seminar on Indian oil and gas which opened in New Delhi on Tuesday. "But how to utilise them is still speculative."
For this reason, he said, he was unable to provide precise details of India's gas hydrate reserves.

Kelkar said gas hydrates formed when methane gas was subjected to extremely low temperatures or very high pressures. The fuel was already being used in a "very small way" in parts of Siberia, he added.

India has pressed its state-run oil companies, as well as the Gas Authority of India and numerous scientific and research institutions, into trying to find ways of exploiting the new fuel source, Kelkar said.
"With their help, we aim to put together a programme to complete exploration within the next five years," Kelkar added.
He said his ministry was drafting contracts for production sharing with commercial exploiters, and expected to circulate model contracts to the industry within "the next few months".
